response_text: Writing and calling C functions offers several advantages. Firstly, C code is more readable and easier to debug with less experience, and coming back to it (for example, in a future lab) for further development is easier compared to assembly. In addition, writing C code tends to be faster for development, and is easier to integrate into the rest of the OS kernel (written in C). However, writing these functions in C allows for less control over the result of the compiled code (compared to assembly which doesn’t need to be compiled because it is just assembly). Additionally, function calls in C introduce more overhead (setting up the registers for the call stack), which is unnecessary work, which could instead be spent running the next thread.\n
